title: WA Telecom Admin — Pretest B
description: 40-question mixed pretest sampling NEC Articles 90, 100–110, 240, 300–398, 705–780, 800–830, RCW 19.28, WAC 296-46B, and general theory. Different questions from Pretest A.

questions.question: NEC Article 90.2 describes the scope of the Code. Which of the following installations is NOT covered by the NEC?
choices: Electrical wiring in a commercial office building
Installations in ships, watercraft, railway rolling stock, and aircraft
Low-voltage communications wiring in a residential building
Solar photovoltaic systems on a residential rooftop
questions.answer: Installations in ships, watercraft, railway rolling stock, and aircraft
questions.explanation: NEC 90.2(B) lists installations not covered by the Code, including ships, watercraft other than floating buildings, railway rolling stock, aircraft, and automotive vehicles — NEC Article 90.

questions.question: NEC Article 90.4 states that the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) has the responsibility to:
choices: Enforce the NEC exactly as written with no discretion
Interpret the NEC and approve equipment, materials, and installations
Issue contractor licenses on behalf of the state
Publish amendments to the NEC every three years
questions.answer: Interpret the NEC and approve equipment, materials, and installations
questions.explanation: NEC 90.4 grants the AHJ the responsibility to interpret the Code requirements, approve equipment and materials, and waive specific requirements or permit alternative methods where equivalent safety is achieved — NEC Article 90.

questions.question: NEC Article 90.7 addresses examination of equipment for safety. Which of the following statements is correct regarding listed equipment?
choices: Listed equipment may never be modified in the field under any circumstances
Equipment that is listed by a nationally recognized testing laboratory (NRTL) is evaluated for compliance with applicable product safety standards
Listing by any organization automatically satisfies all NEC requirements without AHJ review
Field-labeled equipment is prohibited by the NEC
questions.answer: Equipment that is listed by a nationally recognized testing laboratory (NRTL) is evaluated for compliance with applicable product safety standards
questions.explanation: NEC 90.7 and Article 100 establish that listed equipment has been evaluated by a qualified electrical testing laboratory (NRTL) and found to meet applicable safety standards — NEC Article 90.

questions.question: Per NEC Article 100, which of the following best defines 'Concealed' as it applies to wiring methods?
choices: Wiring that is protected by a metal raceway
Wiring rendered inaccessible by the structure or finish of a building
Wiring installed underground
Wiring that is colored gray to blend with the wall surface
questions.answer: Wiring rendered inaccessible by the structure or finish of a building
questions.explanation: NEC Article 100 defines 'Concealed' as rendered inaccessible by the structure or finish of the building. Wires in concealed raceways are considered concealed even though they may be accessible — NEC Article 100.

questions.question: Per NEC Article 100, what is the defined meaning of 'Listed' as applied to electrical equipment?
choices: Equipment that has been approved by the local AHJ only
Equipment that appears in a list published by a nationally recognized testing laboratory and has been evaluated for safety
Equipment manufactured in the United States and bearing a UL mark
Any equipment that the electrical contractor has approved for use on a job site
questions.answer: Equipment that appears in a list published by a nationally recognized testing laboratory and has been evaluated for safety
questions.explanation: NEC Article 100 defines 'Listed' as equipment, materials, or services that have been evaluated by an NRTL and found to meet specific designation criteria — NEC Article 100.

questions.question: NEC Article 100 defines 'Qualified Person.' Which of the following best matches that definition?
choices: Any person who holds a valid electrician's license in any US state
One who has skills and knowledge related to the construction and operation of electrical equipment and installations, and has received safety training to recognize and avoid hazards
A person with at least five years of field experience in electrical construction
Any person employed by a licensed electrical contractor
questions.answer: One who has skills and knowledge related to the construction and operation of electrical equipment and installations, and has received safety training to recognize and avoid hazards
questions.explanation: NEC Article 100 defines a 'Qualified Person' as one who has skills and knowledge of electrical equipment and installations, and has received safety training to recognize and avoid hazards — NEC Article 100.

questions.question: NEC 110.3(B) requires that listed or labeled equipment be:
choices: Painted to match the color code specified by the AHJ
Installed and used in accordance with any instructions included in the listing or labeling
Retested by the contractor before installation
Approved by the engineer of record before the AHJ inspection
questions.answer: Installed and used in accordance with any instructions included in the listing or labeling
questions.explanation: NEC 110.3(B) requires that listed or labeled equipment be installed and used in accordance with the instructions included in the listing or labeling — NEC Article 110.

questions.question: NEC Article 110.26(C) requires that the area above electrical equipment operating at 600 V or less have minimum headroom of:
choices: 6 feet, 3 inches
7 feet
6 feet
8 feet
questions.answer: 6 feet, 3 inches
questions.explanation: NEC 110.26(C) requires a minimum headroom of 6 feet 3 inches (1.9 m) in front of electrical equipment — NEC Article 110.

questions.question: NEC 240.4(D) limits overcurrent protection for 12 AWG copper conductors to a maximum of:
choices: 15 amperes
20 amperes
25 amperes
30 amperes
questions.answer: 20 amperes
questions.explanation: NEC 240.4(D) states that 12 AWG copper conductors shall not be protected by overcurrent devices rated more than 20 amperes — NEC Article 240.

questions.question: Per NEC 240.6(A), which of the following is a standard ampere rating for overcurrent devices?
choices: 22 amperes
45 amperes
55 amperes
85 amperes
questions.answer: 45 amperes
questions.explanation: NEC 240.6(A) lists standard ampere ratings including 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, and higher. 45 A is a listed standard rating — NEC Article 240.

questions.question: NEC Article 240.87 requires arc energy reduction for circuit breakers rated 1,200 amperes or higher. Which of the following is an acceptable method to achieve this?
choices: Installing a time-delay fuse in parallel with the breaker
Zone-selective interlocking, differential relaying, or an energy-reducing active arc flash mitigation system
Adding a manual disconnect within 10 feet of the breaker
Labeling the panel with the available fault current
questions.answer: Zone-selective interlocking, differential relaying, or an energy-reducing active arc flash mitigation system
questions.explanation: NEC 240.87 requires that where the highest continuous current trip setting of a breaker is 1,200 A or higher, a method to reduce clearing time or arc energy must be provided — acceptable methods include zone-selective interlocking and differential relaying — NEC Article 240.

questions.question: NEC Article 240.24(B) prohibits overcurrent devices from being located in which of the following areas?
choices: In commercial kitchens adjacent to cooking equipment
In bathrooms of dwelling units, dormitories, and guest rooms
In utility rooms of commercial buildings
In electrical rooms with a locking door
questions.answer: In bathrooms of dwelling units, dormitories, and guest rooms
questions.explanation: NEC 240.24(B) prohibits overcurrent devices from being installed in the bathrooms of dwelling units, dormitories, and hotel/motel guest rooms — NEC Article 240.

questions.question: NEC Article 300.15 generally requires that a box or fitting be installed at every point where wiring methods join or conductors are spliced. Which of the following is a listed exception?
choices: Conductors spliced within a junction box with a cover
Splices made in conduit bodies (condulets) that are accessible and of a sufficient size
Wire nuts used outside of boxes in finished walls
Splices made in rigid metallic conduit runs longer than 6 feet
questions.answer: Splices made in conduit bodies (condulets) that are accessible and of a sufficient size
questions.explanation: NEC 300.15 requires boxes or fittings at all conductor splices, but permits splices in conduit bodies that are accessible and have sufficient fill volume per NEC 314.16 — NEC Article 300.

questions.question: NEC Article 310.15 governs conductor ampacity. Which of the following factors does NOT affect conductor ampacity?
choices: Ambient temperature
Number of current-carrying conductors in a raceway
Insulation temperature rating of the conductor
The color of the conductor insulation
questions.answer: The color of the conductor insulation
questions.explanation: Conductor ampacity per NEC 310.15 is affected by ambient temperature, number of current-carrying conductors (bundling), and insulation temperature rating — insulation color does not affect ampacity — NEC Article 310.

questions.question: NEC Article 334 covers Nonmetallic-Sheathed Cable (NM/Romex). NM cable is generally permitted to be used in which type of structure?
choices: Buildings exceeding three floors above grade in height
One- and two-family dwellings and other structures permitted by the Code
All commercial occupancies regardless of construction type
Wet and damp locations when protected by a conduit
questions.answer: One- and two-family dwellings and other structures permitted by the Code
questions.explanation: NEC 334.10 permits NM cable in one- and two-family dwellings and multifamily dwellings and other structures where specifically permitted — NEC Article 334.

questions.question: NEC Article 344 covers Rigid Metal Conduit (RMC). In which of the following environments is RMC specifically well suited for use?
choices: Only in dry indoor environments
Exposed, concealed, and in concrete, in contact with earth, and in hazardous locations
Only where embedded in concrete slabs
Only in plenum air-handling spaces
questions.answer: Exposed, concealed, and in concrete, in contact with earth, and in hazardous locations
questions.explanation: NEC 344.10 permits RMC in all atmospheric conditions and occupancies, including direct earth burial, concrete encasement, and hazardous locations — NEC Article 344.

questions.question: NEC Article 352 covers Rigid Polyvinyl Chloride Conduit (PVC). What is a key restriction on the use of Schedule 40 PVC conduit exposed to physical damage?
choices: It is permitted in all exposed locations without restriction
It shall not be used where exposed to physical damage unless identified for that use
It must be painted gray when installed exposed
It requires a metallic inner liner when installed exposed above grade
questions.answer: It shall not be used where exposed to physical damage unless identified for that use
questions.explanation: NEC 352.12 restricts PVC conduit from areas subject to physical damage unless the conduit is specifically identified for such use — NEC Article 352.

questions.question: NEC Article 690.31 governs the wiring methods for PV system DC circuits. Which of the following is required for PV source and output circuit conductors installed on or in buildings?
choices: All PV DC conductors must be installed in rigid metal conduit only
PV conductors shall be identified with a label or marking at all accessible points stating they are solar PV system conductors
PV DC conductors must use aluminum conductors exclusively
PV conductors must be shielded and grounded at both ends
questions.answer: PV conductors shall be identified with a label or marking at all accessible points stating they are solar PV system conductors
questions.explanation: NEC 690.31 requires PV source and output circuit conductors to be identified with markings or labels at accessible points to alert personnel — NEC Article 690.

questions.question: NEC Article 706.10 covers the location of Energy Storage Systems (ESS). Which of the following is a location requirement for ESS equipment?
choices: ESS must always be installed outdoors
ESS must be installed in a dedicated room with a 2-hour fire-rated door
ESS shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's installation instructions and shall be accessible only to qualified persons where required
ESS must be located within 10 feet of the main service panel
questions.answer: ESS shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's installation instructions and shall be accessible only to qualified persons where required
questions.explanation: NEC 706.10 requires ESS to be installed per manufacturer instructions and accessible only to qualified persons where the system presents a shock or arc flash hazard — NEC Article 706.

questions.question: NEC Article 750 covers Energy Management Systems (EMS). What is the primary purpose of an EMS as defined by Article 750?
choices: To limit the voltage on distribution circuits to prevent overvoltage
To monitor and manage electrical loads to prevent exceeding a set demand or to optimize energy use
To automatically disconnect the utility service during peak rate periods
To provide backup power during utility outages
questions.answer: To monitor and manage electrical loads to prevent exceeding a set demand or to optimize energy use
questions.explanation: NEC Article 750 covers Energy Management Systems, which monitor and control loads to manage energy demand and prevent exceeding load limits — NEC Article 750.

questions.question: NEC Article 760 covers Fire Alarm Systems. Which cable type is required for fire alarm circuits installed in a plenum space?
choices: FPLR (Fire Power Limited Riser)
FPL (Fire Power Limited General Purpose)
FPLP (Fire Power Limited Plenum)
FPLS (Fire Power Limited Special)
questions.answer: FPLP (Fire Power Limited Plenum)
questions.explanation: NEC 760.179 and Table 760.179 require FPLP-rated cable for fire alarm circuits installed in plenum air-handling spaces — NEC Article 760.

questions.question: NEC Article 800.53 requires that unlisted communications cables and cables from outside a building be located at least how far from the point of entrance before connecting to listed cables or protected equipment?
choices: 3 feet
50 feet
As close as practicable to the point of entrance
No distance requirement; any point in the building is acceptable
questions.answer: 50 feet
questions.explanation: NEC 800.53 generally limits unlisted outside-plant communications cables to no more than 50 feet inside a building before connecting to listed indoor cables or a primary protector — NEC Article 800.

questions.question: NEC Article 800 classifies communications circuits. Which of the following correctly describes a 'Communications Circuit'?
choices: Any circuit operating above 600 V used for signal transmission
A circuit that transmits voice, data, or video signals and is powered at limited voltage and power levels
A circuit used exclusively for fire alarm signaling
A circuit that supplies power to network switches and routers
questions.answer: A circuit that transmits voice, data, or video signals and is powered at limited voltage and power levels
questions.explanation: NEC Article 800 covers communications circuits — those that transmit voice, audio, data, or video signals at limited energy levels — NEC Article 800.

questions.question: Per NEC Article 820.44, coaxial cable used in CATV systems that is run between floors in a building (in riser shafts) shall be rated at minimum:
choices: CATV (basic grade, general purpose)
CATVP (plenum rated)
CATVR (riser rated)
CATVX (limited use)
questions.answer: CATVR (riser rated)
questions.explanation: NEC 820.179 and Table 820.179 require CATVR-rated coaxial cable for installations in vertical riser shafts — NEC Article 820.

questions.question: NEC Article 830.3 classifies network-powered broadband communications circuits. A 'low power' network-powered broadband circuit is characterized by:
choices: Output power not exceeding 250 VA and 150 V
Output power not exceeding 100 VA and operating at or below 100 V
Output power not exceeding 15 W regardless of voltage
Any circuit delivering power over a coaxial cable
questions.answer: Output power not exceeding 15 W regardless of voltage
questions.explanation: NEC Article 830 classifies low-power network-powered broadband circuits as those where the power output does not exceed 15 W — NEC Article 830.

questions.question: NEC Article 840 covers Premises-Powered Broadband Communications Systems. What distinguishes an Article 840 system from an Article 830 system?
choices: Article 840 covers fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) systems powered from premises equipment rather than from the network
Article 840 covers coaxial-based systems; Article 830 covers fiber-based systems
Article 840 applies only to commercial buildings; Article 830 applies to residences
Article 840 systems require no grounding or bonding
questions.answer: Article 840 covers fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) systems powered from premises equipment rather than from the network
questions.explanation: NEC Article 840 covers premises-powered broadband systems (e.g., FTTH/optical network terminals) where power is supplied by premises equipment rather than from the network provider — NEC Article 840.

questions.question: RCW 19.28.006 defines 'electrical work' for the purposes of the chapter. Which of the following activities is considered 'electrical work' under RCW 19.28?
choices: Replacing a light bulb in a residential fixture
Installing, maintaining, or repairing electrical wiring, devices, appliances, and equipment
Painting an electrical panel enclosure
Cleaning the exterior of an outdoor electrical disconnect
questions.answer: Installing, maintaining, or repairing electrical wiring, devices, appliances, and equipment
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.006 defines 'electrical work' broadly to include installing, maintaining, or repairing electrical wiring, devices, appliances, and equipment — RCW 19.28.006.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28, a homeowner may perform electrical work on their own single-family residence under which condition?
choices: The homeowner must first pass a written electrical exam administered by L&I
The homeowner must obtain the required permit and the work must be inspected by L&I
No permit or inspection is required for homeowner work
The homeowner must be supervised by a licensed journeyman electrician
questions.answer: The homeowner must obtain the required permit and the work must be inspected by L&I
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28 allows a homeowner to perform electrical work on their own single-family dwelling, but a permit must be obtained and the work is subject to L&I inspection — RCW 19.28.

questions.question: RCW 19.28.191 requires that all electrical contractors in Washington State maintain which of the following before performing electrical work?
choices: A surety bond and certificate of insurance
Only a business license from the city
A letter of authorization from the local utility
A blanket permit from L&I covering all projects statewide
questions.answer: A surety bond and certificate of insurance
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.191 requires electrical contractors to file a surety bond and maintain a certificate of insurance as a condition of licensure — RCW 19.28.191.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28, which of the following accurately describes the difference between a 'telecommunications contractor' license and a 'telecommunications administrator' certificate?
choices: They are identical credentials used interchangeably
The contractor license is held by the business entity; the administrator certificate is held by the individual responsible for supervising the work
The administrator certificate allows the individual to own and operate a business; the contractor license allows field installation only
The contractor license is issued by the city; the administrator certificate is issued by the state
questions.answer: The contractor license is held by the business entity; the administrator certificate is held by the individual responsible for supervising the work
questions.explanation: Under RCW 19.28, the telecommunications contractor license is a business license; the telecommunications administrator certificate is held by the qualifying individual who supervises and is responsible for the contractor's work — RCW 19.28.

questions.question: RCW 19.28.401 establishes an electrical board. What is the primary function of this board?
choices: To conduct final inspections in lieu of L&I
To advise the director of L&I on matters relating to electrical licensing, training, and safety
To set utility rates for electrical service
To approve all electrical permit applications in the state
questions.answer: To advise the director of L&I on matters relating to electrical licensing, training, and safety
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.401 establishes an electrical board that advises the director of L&I on licensing standards, training requirements, and electrical safety matters — RCW 19.28.401.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28, a telecommunications contractor who allows their license to lapse and continues to perform work may be subject to:
choices: Only a written reprimand
Civil fines, license revocation, and a stop-work order
Referral to the electrical board for mediation only
A requirement to retake the administrator exam
questions.answer: Civil fines, license revocation, and a stop-work order
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28 authorizes L&I to impose civil fines, revoke licenses, and issue stop-work orders for contractors performing work without a current, valid license — RCW 19.28.

questions.question: WAC 296-46B establishes the process for third-party electrical inspections in Washington. Under what circumstances may a third-party inspection agency be used in lieu of L&I inspections?
choices: Third-party inspections are never permitted in Washington State
When the project owner requests it and the third-party agency is certified by L&I
Only for projects exceeding $1 million in electrical work
Only for work performed by licensed master electricians
questions.answer: When the project owner requests it and the third-party agency is certified by L&I
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B allows certified third-party electrical inspection agencies to perform inspections in lieu of L&I, provided the agency is certified and the process is followed — WAC 296-46B.

questions.question: WAC 296-46B specifies how electrical permits are obtained in Washington. Which of the following is a required step before an electrical permit is issued?
choices: Submission of stamped engineered drawings for all residential projects
Completion of the permit application with a description of the work and payment of the applicable fee
Approval from the local fire marshal before L&I issues the permit
A pre-construction meeting with the L&I inspector
questions.answer: Completion of the permit application with a description of the work and payment of the applicable fee
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B requires that an electrical permit application describing the scope of work be submitted and fees paid before the permit is issued — WAC 296-46B.

questions.question: WAC 296-46B addresses the qualifications for telecommunications administrator applicants. Which of the following is a general prerequisite for obtaining a telecommunications administrator certificate in Washington?
choices: A minimum of 10 years of field experience as a licensed journeyman electrician
Passing the telecommunications administrator examination and meeting experience or education requirements
Holding a professional engineer (PE) license
Completion of a 4-year electrical engineering degree
questions.answer: Passing the telecommunications administrator examination and meeting experience or education requirements
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B requires applicants for a telecommunications administrator certificate to pass the required examination and meet applicable experience or education requirements — WAC 296-46B.

questions.question: WAC 296-46B specifies work that may be performed by a trainee telecommunications worker. Which of the following is accurate regarding trainee work?
choices: Trainees may work independently without supervision on any telecommunications project
Trainees must work under the direct supervision of a certified telecommunications administrator or qualified supervisor
Trainees are prohibited from performing any work until they pass the administrator exam
Trainees may supervise other trainees if they have more than one year of experience
questions.answer: Trainees must work under the direct supervision of a certified telecommunications administrator or qualified supervisor
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B requires that telecommunications trainees work under the direct supervision of a qualified, certified administrator or supervisor — WAC 296-46B.

questions.question: WAC 296-46B addresses situations where an electrical installation fails inspection. What is the required process after a failed inspection?
choices: The contractor may energize the installation and re-request inspection within 30 days
The deficiencies cited must be corrected and a re-inspection requested before the installation may be energized or covered
A written appeal must be filed within 5 days or the permit is revoked
The contractor may correct the deficiency and self-certify without a re-inspection
questions.answer: The deficiencies cited must be corrected and a re-inspection requested before the installation may be energized or covered
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B requires that deficiencies noted during an inspection be corrected and a re-inspection be scheduled; the installation shall not be energized or concealed until it passes — WAC 296-46B.

questions.question: Under WAC 296-46B, what is the consequence if an electrical permit expires before inspections are completed?
choices: The work is automatically approved if no violations were noted at rough-in
A new permit must be obtained and associated fees paid before work may continue
The contractor receives a 12-month automatic extension at no charge
The permit expiration has no legal effect on the installation
questions.answer: A new permit must be obtained and associated fees paid before work may continue
questions.explanation: WAC 296-46B requires that a new permit be obtained if the original permit expires before all required inspections are completed — WAC 296-46B.

questions.question: A capacitive load causes the current waveform to do which of the following relative to the voltage waveform?
choices: Lag voltage by 90°
Remain in phase with voltage
Lead voltage
Lead voltage by exactly 180°
questions.answer: Lead voltage
questions.explanation: In a capacitive load, current leads voltage because the capacitor charges before the voltage reaches its peak. This is opposite to the behavior of an inductive load — General Theory (AC Phase Relationships).

questions.question: In a star (point-to-point) network topology used in structured cabling, all end devices connect to a central device such as a switch or hub. What is a primary advantage of this topology compared to a bus topology?
choices: A single cable failure disables all devices on the network
It requires less cable than a bus topology for the same number of devices
A failure in one cable link affects only that individual device, not the rest of the network
All devices share a single transmission medium, reducing total cost
questions.answer: A failure in one cable link affects only that individual device, not the rest of the network
questions.explanation: In a star topology, each device has a dedicated link to the central switch; a single link failure isolates only that device, leaving the rest of the network operational — General Theory (Network Topology).
